sections.overview: The Comma Nephele is an African hawkmoth in the family Sphingidae.
sections.identification: Its forewing commonly bears a small pale, comma-shaped mark, although the reported form derasa lacks it.
sections.habitat: Regional species records place it widely across sub-Saharan Africa and nearby islands.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on several woody plants, including species of Carissa and Landolphia.
sections.behavior: The sources consulted document its appearance and range more clearly than its daily behavior.
sections.reproduction: The species accounts consulted do not provide enough verified detail to summarize its breeding cycle.
sections.ecology: It belongs to a diverse African genus; no close relative with a completed profile in this catalogue was found for a direct comparison.
sections.conservation: The sources reviewed do not establish a global population trend or conservation category for this species.
